Task T3 is complete. Summary of what's in `runs/advisor/t3-claude/`:

**Core deliverables** (as specified in the brief):
- `script.R` — self-contained, reproducible R script (seeded, Okabe-Ito palette)
- `sensitivity-table.md` — crime AMCEs under both baselines (2×2), housing-cost AMCEs under all 3 baselines, and MMs for all 24 levels
- `figures/sensitivity.png` — one figure: all 24 levels' marginal means, faceted by attribute, ordered by descending MM range, 2304×2432px @ 320 dpi, no title
- `memo.md` — 427-word reply to the reviewer

**Process artifacts** (advisor-arm convention): I solved the brief directly, then consulted Fable 5 (via `fable-advisor.sh`, one delegation) as an independent reviewer, and ran one revision pass. The consult caught a real problem worth flagging: my first draft asserted crime had "the largest" MM spread while separately promising not to claim crime was "the largest or most important attribute" — a genuine internal contradiction, since the crime/commuting-time gap (0.014) isn't statistically sharp. It also caught a wording error (a 3-level attribute reports 2 AMCEs per baseline, not "the single AMCE") and correctly flagged that my original two-panel figure (crime + housing) didn't actually display the evidence for the memo's comparative claim. I fixed all three and added a stronger baseline-free rebuttal the advisor suggested: since any AMCE is just a difference of two MMs, no re-baselining of any attribute can produce a value exceeding crime's own MM range — so crime's position at the top is invariant to reference coding, even though its lead over commuting time isn't precise. `briefing.md`, `advice.md`, `run-log.md`, and `SHA256SUMS` document that process.
